summary: Monterey County, CA lookout on Santa Lucia (Junipero Serra) Peak, built 1935; cabin removed, tower remains; Forest Service listed the trail to it closed in Aug 2026.

facts.design: 30-foot K-brace open steel tower with a California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin; wood cab per Forest Lookouts
facts.status_note: Tower remains but the cabin was removed at an unknown date. A hiking blog calls the site a ruin abandoned in 1979; not confirmed.
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Los Padres National Forest

access.note: Reached on foot through the Ventana Wilderness. Forest Service lists the Santa Lucia Peak Trail (6E01) closed as of Aug 2026 after the Timber and Plaskett fires.

visit.trail_note: 2.3-mile trail forks from the Santa Lucia Trail (5E03). No motorized use in wilderness; no wilderness permits issued. Closed per Forest Service page; do not attempt the tower.

events.note: Register gives 1935 as the build year; Forest Lookouts says the CCC constructed it
Only a hiking blog gives this date; not in the Register or Forest Lookouts, unconfirmed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on December 20, 2019

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Our record lists the tower as standing while another list says ruins. The Register says the tower remains and only the cabin is gone, so the tower is standing. The hiking blog's ruin description and 1979 date are unconfirmed.
Sources use two names for the summit: the Register says Santa Lucia Peak and the Forest Service trail page says Junipero Serra Peak. Both name the same lookout site.

notes_for_editor: No staffing or notable fire found in the pages read. Brief's access was unknown; now closed per the Forest Service page dated Aug 2026, so recheck. Peakbagging.com (search snippet only, not read) reports the cab gone in 2001 photos; a lead for dating the cab removal. The 1979 date rests on one blog. Brief's 'fflos=gone' conflict is the cabin, not the tower.
